title: Linear structures of the APN differential-spectrum function
summary: Determine whether the Boolean function associated with an APN differential spectrum has nonzero linear structures.

formal_statement.body: Let $F:\mathbb F_2^n\to\mathbb F_2^n$ be APN and let $\gamma_F(a,b)=1$ exactly when $F(x+a)+F(x)=b$ has a solution. For the source-defined even-dimensional case, determine all linear structures of $\gamma_F$ (in particular, whether a nonzero structure of the form $(0,\beta)$ exists). Prove nonexistence or characterize every such structure for general APN $F$.

scope.domain: APN vectorial Boolean functions and the Boolean differential-spectrum function $\gamma_F$
assumptions: $F$ is APN under the source definition
$n$ is even for the nonzero-structure subproblem
$\gamma_F$ is defined from the differential spectrum
scope.unresolved_remainder: The plateaued APN subclass is settled in even dimensions. A complete existence/nonexistence result and characterization remains open for non-plateaued APN functions in the source's even-dimensional domain.

progress.summary: The TIT source explicitly states this unresolved problem and fixes its mathematical scope.
Proposition 7.2 proves that gamma_F has no nontrivial linear structures when n is even and F is plateaued APN; non-plateaued APN functions remain outside the theorem.
